battle.name: 普法戰爭
battle.brief: 1870年7月19日法國向普魯士與北德邦聯宣戰，戰線自洛林推向巴黎盆地，年初轉為巴黎圍城。卡面這門1850年代的線膛前膛野戰砲，正是當時歐洲砲兵的標準配備：刻膛線讓同樣的藥量走得更遠；但同一場戰役裡，它正面撞上克魯伯的鋼製後膛砲，射程差距最終把法軍從洛林逼回巴黎。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 普法戰爭在1870年7月19日開打，交戰的兩邊並非單一國家，而是兩套聯邦體系。北方是北德意志邦聯：核心為普魯士王國，另有薩克森、巴伐利亞、符騰堡、巴登與黑森-達姆施塔特等邦的分遣隊編入聯邦軍，1871年1月18日聯邦改組為德意志帝國，威廉一世即皇帝位。普軍最高指揮為國王兼總司令威廉一世，參謀總長老毛奇負責全軍戰略計畫，國防部長羅恩主持軍制與後勤，宰相俾斯麥掌外交並以「埃姆斯電報」決定開戰時機；前線編制分為第一軍、第二軍與第三軍，第三軍由弗里德里希·卡爾親王率領，另有由南德各邦混編的美因河軍與默茲河軍兩個整編單位。法國方面是拿破崙三世統治的第二帝國，其野戰兵力雖號稱歐洲最強，但部隊以團、旅為單位分散駐紮，軍需與後勤集中於少數鐵路樞紐；帝國陸軍由麥克馬洪、巴贊內、康羅貝等元帥分領萊茵河軍各軍團，戰時因營級缺編、砲兵不足與遠程小口徑砲缺員而難以集中火力。9月4日第二帝國垮台之後，共和派在巴黎成立國防政府，由特羅居元帥任軍事總督、朱爾·法夫爾主持對外談判，並組織國民守備軍與新編的野戰軍，法軍先後組成羅瓦河軍、東方軍與安貝爾-索恩軍，對德軍發動冬季反攻；德方則要提防法國可能的普世同盟、義大利志願兵與英國的觀望，於是始終避免與其他大國正面交鋒。整體而言，這是一場聯邦軍對帝國軍、共和軍再對聯邦軍的兩段式戰爭，軸心落在洛林、萊茵河下游與巴黎盆地。
countriesEn: The Franco-Prussian War broke out on 19 July 1870, and the two sides were not single states but two federal systems. To the north stood the North German Confederation, with the Kingdom of Prussia at its core and contingents from Saxony, Bavaria, Württemberg, Baden and Hesse-Darmstadt folded into the federal army; on 18 January 1871 the Confederation was refounded as the German Empire, with Wilhelm I as its emperor. On the Prussian side the supreme command belonged to the king, who was also commander-in-chief in the field. Chief of the General Staff Helmuth von Moltke the Elder drew up the strategic plan, War Minister Albrecht von Roon ran the army system and the logistics, and Chancellor Otto von Bismarck handled foreign affairs and, through the Ems Dispatch, decided the moment the war would break out. The field force was organised into the First Army, the Second Army and the Third Army, the last commanded by Prince Friedrich Karl, together with the Army of the Meuse and the Army of the South German contingents. France was Napoleon III's Second Empire. Its peacetime field army was said to be the strongest in Europe, but the troops were dispersed in small garrisons, and the commissariat and the transport were concentrated at a handful of railway junctions. The imperial army was divided among the corps of the Army of the Rhine commanded by marshals such as MacMahon, Bazaine and Canrobert, and its inability to concentrate, caused by missing battalion depots, insufficient artillery and shortages of long-range light pieces, was to prove fatal. After the fall of the Empire on 4 September 1870, the republicans set up a Government of National Defence in Paris, with Marshal Trochu as military governor and Jules Favre conducting the negotiations, and they raised the National Guard and new field armies to fight the Confederation: an Army of the Loire, an Army of the East around Bourbaki, and an Army of the Vosges. Germany had to face the possibility of a general European coalition, of Italian volunteers and of British and Russian neutrality, and so it avoided any confrontation with the other great powers. In short, this was a two-stage war, federal armies against the imperial army and then republican armies against the federal ones, fought along the frontier in Lorraine, along the lower Rhine and in the basin of Paris.
people: 這場戰爭的關鍵人物集中在普魯士一側。威廉一世以國王身分兼任總司令，宣戰當日自埃姆斯趕回柏林，在軍營中接納老毛奇與俾斯麥的方案。參謀總長老毛奇是全軍的大腦：他把動員程序、鐵路運輸與數路大軍的分割行軍揉成一份計畫，讓德軍沿邊境山脊後方展開，由各路在色當會合，避免逐次與法軍主力遭遇。國防部長羅恩代表軍制一面，普軍的兵員、訓練與後勤正是他十年改革與參謀專業化的產物。宰相俾斯麥則決定戰爭何時爆發：他把威廉一世與法使貝特曼在埃姆斯的談話改寫成一份傷及法國面子的公告，激怒巴黎輿論；色當勝利當日他在凡爾賽宣讀德意志帝國的成立，9月30日在帝國議會說出「鐵與血」一語，承認這場戰爭不是演武，而是由鐵與血鑄成。第三軍司令弗里德里希·卡爾親王是色當的實際贏家，他主張直取法軍的中央陣位，法軍全軍因此被切斷。第九軍團長扎比洛夫斯基在馬斯拉圖爾以劣勢兵力拖住法軍主力，為全軍展開換來關鍵時間。法國方面的關鍵人物是拿破崙三世本人，他以歐洲軍力第二的自信誤判形勢，成為色當的俘虜；麥克馬洪元帥指揮的萊茵河軍被合圍之後，他於9月4日與巴黎通電，促成帝國退位；巴贊內元帥接任萊茵河軍司令，卻在梅茲被圍後於10月27日率約十萬人投降，成為法軍史上最大的單次投降。共和國一方，以朱爾·法夫爾負責對德談判、費里組織守備與游擊、軍事總督特羅居主持巴黎防禦最為人知；加利尼與杜克羅在香佩尼與埃唐普的堅持，萊沃在塞納河下游的抵抗，以及布爾巴基元帥率東方軍在冬季反攻中於貝爾福與埃里庫爾被默茲河軍擊潰的結局，共同構成共和國最艱難的一頁。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities of this war sat on the Prussian side. Wilhelm I was king and commander-in-chief in the field, and on the day of the declaration he hurried back from Ems to Berlin, where he accepted the plan drawn up by Moltke and Bismarck. Chief of the General Staff Helmuth von Moltke the Elder was the brain of the army: he fused mobilisation, rail transport and the marching of separate armies into a single plan that deployed the German force behind the frontier ridges and brought the columns together at Sedan, so as never to meet the main French army piecemeal. War Minister Albrecht von Roon stood for the army system itself, and the manpower, training and logistics of the Prussian army were the product of his decade of reform and of professional staff work. Chancellor Otto von Bismarck decided when the war would start: he rewrote the conversation between Wilhelm I and the French ambassador Benedetti at Ems into a communiqué that humiliated France and inflamed opinion in Paris, and on the day of the victory at Sedan he announced the German Empire; on 30 September he told the Reichstag that the war was no display of arms but was forged from iron and blood. Prince Friedrich Karl, commander of the Third Army, was the practical victor at Sedan, insisting on striking the French centre so that the whole enemy army was cut in two. Gebhard von Zabylowski, commanding the IX Corps, held the French main force at Mars-la-Tour with inferior numbers and bought the time the whole army needed to deploy. On the French side the central figure was Napoleon III himself, who misjudged the situation with the confidence of the second military power in Europe and ended up a prisoner at Sedan. Marshal MacMahon, whose Army of the Rhine was enclosed, telegraphed Paris on 4 September and the Empire fell; Marshal Bazaine, who took over the Army of the Rhine, surrendered about a hundred thousand men at Metz on 27 October, the largest single surrender in the history of the French army. On the republican side the best known figures were Jules Favre for the negotiations with Germany, Ferry for organising the defence and the francs-tireurs, and Trochu, the military governor who directed the defence of Paris; to them belong Gallieni and Ducrot at Champigny and Étreux, the resistance of Loewenthal along the lower Seine, and the fate of Bourbaki's Army of the East, broken by the Army of the Meuse around Belfort and Héricourt in the winter offensive.
kits: 卡面上是1850年前後德意志諸邦普遍列裝的線膛前膛野戰砲：普魯士的六磅八十七毫米線膛銅砲、法國與南德邦的四磅八十毫米及九〇毫米線膛砲，都屬同一類。它的原理並不複雜，在炮膛內刻出螺旋膛線，改用橢圓形或截錐形的前膛藥包與帶鉛心的彈丸，同樣一包藥就能把射程從球形實心彈的三四百步推到一千步以上，砲兵第一次可以在射程上壓過步兵；但前膛裝填意味著每發都要重新裝藥、退膛、擦膛，銅砲的膛線又會被殘渣與彈帶磨損，射速低、射界固定、而且無法在掩體內快速反擊。普法戰役正是這門砲最後一次大規模服役，而且它是在被自己的後繼者包圍的狀態下打的：戰役開打時，普軍野戰砲主力已換成克魯伯鋼製後膛砲（六磅八十七毫米與一二磅一百二十毫米），法軍主力換成德邦式後膛砲，線膛前膛砲退到後備砲隊、攻城營壘、要塞與砲位守備上。真正決定會戰的兩件步槍也屬後膛家族：一是普軍針發後膛步槍，一八六二年型與一八六六年型，二是法軍沙士孢一八六六年式後膛步槍，後者的瞄準射速標稱每分鐘十發，常被視為遠超對手，是格萊維洛特與色當兩役中最出名的變數。砲兵對決同樣偏向鋼質後膛：普軍配備克魯伯一五公分野戰砲、二一與二四公分攻城砲，以及射程四公里以上、彈重逾二百五十公斤的二八公分大口徑攻城砲；法軍則有德邦式二四〇毫米攻城砲與一五五毫米野戰砲。攻城器材上，普軍自帶攻城塔、壕溝工具、地雷與臼砲，並在巴黎圍城末段以八十七門長射程克魯伯砲從五十五至七十五公里外轟擊市區；後勤上普軍以鐵路、民車與軍用麵包維持空前規模的遠征，法軍則靠要塞囤糧與市場徵購，漸至無以為繼。
kitsEn: On the card face is a rifled muzzle-loading field gun of the kind widely issued by the German states around 1850: the Prussian six-pounder of 87 mm rifled bronze, and the French and southern German four-pounder of 80 mm and 90 mm all belong to the same family. The principle is simple: a spiral groove cut into the bore, combined with an elongated or truncated-conical front-loading charge and a projectile with a lead core, allows the same quantity of powder to carry a full three or four hundred paces further than a round shot, and for the first time artillery could outrange infantry in range. The cost is that a front-loading gun must be loaded, sponged and cleared after every round, that the bronze rifling wears away under fouling and driving bands, and that the rate of fire is low, the arc of fire fixed, and no immediate counter-battery reply possible from cover. The war of 1870 and 1871 was the last great campaign in which this gun saw large-scale service, and it was fought while already being overtaken by its own successor: when the war opened, the Prussian field artillery had already gone over to Krupp steel breech-loading guns, the six-pounder of 87 mm and the twelve-pounder of 120 mm, and the French field artillery to the de Bange breech-loader, so that the rifled muzzle-loader was pushed back into reserve batteries, siege trains, fortresses and gun positions. The two infantry weapons that actually decided the battles were also breech-loaders: the Prussian needle gun of 1862 and 1866, and the French Chassepot rifle of 1866, whose advertised aimed rate of fire of ten rounds a minute was widely treated as far beyond anything the enemy could match and which became the best known variable at Gravelotte and Sedan. The artillery duel leaned the same way, towards steel breech-loaders: the Prussians brought Krupp 15 cm field pieces, 21 and 24 cm siege guns and a heavy 28 cm piece of more than 250 kg with a range above four kilometres, while the French had the de Bange 240 mm siege gun and the 155 mm field piece. On siege equipment the Prussians carried towers, sap tools, mines and heavy mortars, and in the last weeks of the siege of Paris they bombarded the city with eighty-seven long-range Krupp guns firing from between fifty-five and seventy-five kilometres; in logistics the Prussians sustained an unprecedented campaign with railways, requisitioned carts and field bakery, while the French depended on fortresses full of grain and on market purchases until those too ran out.
tactics: 德軍的戰術核心是分散行軍、集中會戰。全軍分成數支獨立大軍沿不同路線前進，行軍縱隊之間刻意留出數小時縱距，宿營地不許接連成長線，使各路能在兩三百里的範圍內獨立機動，敵人無法一次接觸全軍；補給由鐵路車隊跟進，步兵縱隊之間保持縱距，砲兵則以營為單位逐次展開，一次集中一個營的火力壓制敵砲位。接近戰場後，德軍的進攻有明確程序：步兵以營為單位躍進，先以散兵線前出，抵近三四百米後再以躍進射擊隊形一躍躍進，每次躍進約一百五十至二百米，行進中交替前進與臥倒射擊，砲火一停即步兵躍進，直到敵陣被切碎。攻擊的重點是敵軍的縱隊與交通線而非全面消耗：馬斯拉圖爾是扎比洛夫斯基用一個軍團在正面拖住法軍，色當則是三路縱隊同時收攏、二十餘個騎兵中隊封鎖缺口，把法軍八萬餘人鎖在盆地裡連續激戰六小時，最後整軍投降。德軍在爾後的會戰中大量使用防禦性展開，把步兵散在塹壕、農舍、果園與圍牆後，利用地形遮蔽反擊。守方法軍在環形陣地中把砲兵集中成一個巨大砲兵群，步兵營散開成射擊線並交替掩蔽，卻因各營之間缺乏縱深而常被德軍一次吃掉一整營。進攻時德軍以連續前進的散兵線與連續躍進提供相互掩護，砲兵靠備用砲與觀察所指揮火力轉移。補給線上，遠征的德軍依賴萊茵河與摩澤爾河畔的鐵路、徵用民車與軍用麵包連鎖供給，離開鐵路後的臨時徵糧極為吃力；巴黎守軍靠要塞糧秣與市集配給，到圍城後期連軍用麵包都成為定量配給品，全軍士氣崩潰。共和政府的冬季反攻則試圖以連續出擊拉平戰局，香佩尼的頭號陣地、埃唐普的防守戰與莫茲河畔的冬季陣地，都是用工事與夜襲拖住德軍的典型做法。
tacticsEn: The core of German doctrine was to march separately and to fight in concentration. The army was split into independent armies advancing on different routes, with hours of interval deliberately left between marching columns and with bivouacs never allowed to string out into a single line, so that each column could manoeuvre independently over a range of two or three hundred kilometres and the enemy could never engage the whole army at once; supply was carried up by railway trains, the interval between infantry columns was kept open, and the artillery was deployed battery by battery, concentrating the fire of one battery at a time against the enemy guns. On approach to the battlefield the German attack followed a set procedure: the infantry advanced by battalion in leapfrog, first pushing forward skirmishers, and at three hundred to four hundred metres the line began fire-and-movement advances, each bound covering a hundred and fifty to two hundred metres, with men alternately going forward and lying down to shoot; when the artillery fire lifted, the infantry bounded forward, until the enemy position was cut to pieces. The weight of the attack fell on the enemy columns and lines of communication rather than on general attrition: Mars-la-Tour was Zabylowski holding the French main effort frontally with a single corps, and Sedan was three columns closing at once while more than twenty cavalry squadrons sealed the gap, locking some eighty thousand Frenchmen in the basin and beating them for six hours before the army surrendered intact. In the later engagements the Germans made heavy use of the extended deployment, scattering infantry in trenches, farmsteads, orchards and behind walls so that the terrain covered their counter-attacks. The French, on the defensive, massed their artillery into a single huge group on the ring positions and opened the infantry into firing lines with alternating cover, but the absence of depth between battalions meant that the Germans frequently swallowed a whole battalion at a time. During the assault mutual cover came from continuous advance of the skirmish line and from repeated bounds, while the artillery shifted fire under the direction of observation posts and reserve guns. On the line of supply the campaigning German army depended on the railways along the Rhine and the Moselle, on requisitioned carts and on field bakeries chained together, and the improvised collection of food away from the rail was hard going; the garrison of Paris relied on fortress stocks and market allocations, and in the late stages even field bread became a rationed item and the morale of the garrison collapsed. The winter offensive of the republican government tried to level the situation by continuous attacks, the first line at Champigny, the defence at Étreux and the winter positions along the Meuse being typical attempts to hold the Germans with field works and night attacks.
data: 時間上，戰爭自1870年7月19日法國宣戰起，至1871年1月28日停戰生效，1月18日德意志帝國宣告成立，5月10日簽訂凡爾賽和約，前線戰鬥歷時約六個多月。兵力方面，北德邦聯動員的總兵力約一百二十萬至一百三十萬，另有大量後備役與地方民兵補入；法軍在戰前的野戰兵力約三十四萬，第一批投入萊茵戰線者不足二十萬，陣亡與被俘之後靠新立國民守備軍與各省守備隊重建。各役數字有明顯差異，一般常見的估計是：德軍陣亡約四萬五千、負傷約十三萬、失蹤約二萬餘；法軍陣亡約十四萬、負傷約二十一萬、被俘約三十二萬，另有一批死於傷病的數字分散在各役。色當一役最常被引用：法軍被圍約八萬三千至十萬人，陣亡約四千、負傷約一萬四，被俘約十萬四千人，拿破崙三世與大批將校同在其中。梅茲圍城自8月13日至10月27日，約十四萬法軍被圍，最後投降者約十萬四千人，圍城期間死於傷病者逾兩萬。巴黎圍城自9月19日至翌年1月28日，被圍者約四十萬至五十萬，軍中因傷病與糧秣不足而死者逾兩萬，配給與糧食供應在冬季降到最低。武器數字亦有參考：沙士孢一八六六年式標稱瞄準射速每分鐘十發，實戰常見約四至五發；針發步槍有效射程約四百米，標稱每分鐘四至五發；克魯伯二八公分攻城砲射程約四公里半，炮彈重逾二百五十公斤；1871年1月轟擊巴黎的長射程砲兵為八十七門克魯伯砲，最大射距達五十五至七十五公里。和約的數字是：割讓亞爾薩斯與洛林的一部分，賠款五十億法郎，佔軍維持到1873年。此外，巴黎在戰前雖已著手要塞改造，棱堡系統尚未完成，這一點直接影響了城防部署的薄弱。
dataEn: In time, the war ran from the French declaration of war on 19 July 1870 to the entry into force of the armistice on 28 January 1871; the German Empire was proclaimed on 18 January and the Treaty of Versailles was signed on 10 May, so that the fighting proper lasted a little over six months. In manpower, the North German Confederation mobilised a total of roughly 1.2 to 1.3 million men, with large numbers of reservists and Landwehr filling the ranks; the French field army numbered about 340,000 men on the eve of the war, fewer than 200,000 of whom were put into the Rhine front at first, and the army was rebuilt after the losses and the captures by the newly raised National Guard and the departmental guards. Figures for the individual battles vary considerably; the estimates most commonly given are about 45,000 German dead, 130,000 wounded and more than 20,000 missing, against about 140,000 French dead, 210,000 wounded and 320,000 captured, with a further number scattered across the campaigns as deaths from wounds and disease. The figures most often quoted for Sedan are that some 83,000 to 100,000 Frenchmen were encircled, about 4,000 killed and 14,000 wounded, and about 104,000 taken prisoner, Napoleon III and a large part of the general staff among them. The siege of Metz lasted from 13 August to 27 October with about 140,000 French troops enclosed; the number who surrendered was about 104,000, and more than 20,000 died of wounds and disease during the siege. The siege of Paris ran from 19 September to 28 January with some 400,000 to 500,000 people enclosed, more than 20,000 military dead from wounds, sickness and shortage, and allocations and food supply fell to their lowest point in the winter. The weapon figures are equally instructive: the Chassepot of 1866 was advertised at ten aimed rounds a minute, with four to five being typical in practice; the needle gun had an effective range of about 400 metres and was rated at four to five rounds a minute; the 28 cm Krupp siege gun had a range of about four and a half kilometres and a shell of more than 250 kg; and the long-range battery that bombarded Paris in January 1871 consisted of eighty-seven Krupp guns at distances of fifty-five to seventy-five kilometres. The treaty figures are: cession of Alsace and part of Lorraine, an indemnity of five billion francs, and occupation of French territory until 1873. It should also be noted that although work had begun on the fortification of Paris before the war, the modern bastion system was still incomplete, which directly weakened the defence of the capital.
cause: 普法戰爭的起因是一連串歐洲外交與軍事事件，最後才落到1870年7月一場誰先動手的選擇上。1864年，普魯士與奧地利聯手打敗丹麥，取得石勒蘇益格與荷爾斯泰因；1866年普奧戰爭，普魯士以速決戰勝奧地利，解散德意志邦聯並吞漢諾威等邦；1867年北德意志邦聯成立，德國統一的路線第一次出現在歐洲外交桌上，普法實力對比被徹底改寫。法國既有的歐陸地位隨之動搖，巴黎既不能容忍普魯士主導德國，也無法再像1850年代那樣拉攏另一個王朝制衡。中立國西班牙的皇位繼承問題成了導火線：1870年，普王的遠房親戚霍亨索倫-西格馬林根家族的萊奧波德在法、西等列強擁護下接受西班牙王位；俾斯麥起初並不反感，後來嗅到法國不會善罷甘休，於是佯裝反對，又放風給法國，主動刺激巴黎出手。法國內部，歐仁·勒讓的報紙與民族主義輿論要求在歐洲事務上不能再退讓；拿破崙三世與歐仁妮皇后的身邊聚集著好戰派，認定對普魯士一戰可以轉移第二帝國內部的社會不滿、恢復王朝聲望；俾斯麥編輯的「埃姆斯電報」把威廉一世與法使貝特曼的談話改寫成一份帶有羞辱色彩的公告，成為巴黎街頭最直接的導火線。法國還有嚴重的低估：1866年普奧戰爭時按兵不動，失去干涉的機會；1867年對普魯士的兼併幾乎照單全收；1870年對西班牙王位問題遲遲不動手，直到埃姆斯談判破裂才倉促宣戰，動員計畫、軍需徵集與營級後備都沒有完成。於是1870年7月19日，法國正式向普魯士與北德邦聯宣戰，這場由一次外交誤判引發的全面戰爭就此開始。
causeEn: The origins of the Franco-Prussian War lie in a chain of European diplomatic and military events, which only at the very end came down to a single choice about who would move first in July 1870. In 1864 Prussia and Austria together defeated Denmark and took Schleswig and Holstein; in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866 Prussia beat Austria in a swift decision, dissolved the German Confederation and absorbed Hanover and other states; in 1867 the North German Confederation was founded, and for the first time the road to German unification lay openly on the European diplomatic table, rewriting the balance of strength between France and Prussia. France's position on the continent was shaken as a result: Paris could neither tolerate a Prussia leading Germany nor find, as in the 1850s, another dynasty to hold in check. The succession to the vacant Spanish throne became the fuse. In 1870 Leopold of the Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen branch of the royal family, a distant relative of the Prussian king, accepted the Spanish crown with the backing of France, Spain and other powers; Bismarck was at first not opposed, but he soon scented that France would not take it lying down, and so he pretended to withdraw the candidacy while deliberately feeding the story to Paris and goading the French into a move. Inside France, the newspapers of Eugène Legrand and the nationalist press insisted that no further retreat be conceded on European affairs; the circles around Napoleon III and the Empress Eugénie were hawkish, convinced that a war against Prussia would divert the social discontent of the Second Empire and restore the prestige of the dynasty; and the Ems Dispatch, edited by Bismarck, turned the conversation between Wilhelm I and the French ambassador Benedetti into a communiqué carrying an unmistakable note of humiliation, which was the most immediate spark in the streets of Paris. France had also miscalculated badly: it had stood aside in 1866 and lost the chance to intervene; in 1867 it had swallowed the annexation of southern German states almost without protest; in 1870 it did nothing over the Spanish candidacy until the talks at Ems broke down, and then declared war in haste, with the mobilisation plan, the requisition of supplies and the battalion reserves all incomplete. Accordingly on 19 July 1870 France formally declared war on Prussia and the North German Confederation, and the general war set off by a single diplomatic misjudgement began.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果遠遠超過歐洲的疆界。第一是政體更替：拿破崙三世被俘、第二帝國在9月4日垮台，法國進入第三共和國，國防政府、特羅居的軍政總督、1871年3月的巴黎公社與隨後的鎮壓，以及1871年的憲法與1873年的總統選舉，共和政體由此定型。第二是歐洲權力地圖改寫：1871年1月18日德意志帝國在凡爾賽鏡廳宣告成立，普魯士王成為德皇，一個以萊茵重工業、鐵路與普魯士式軍隊為骨架的新強權出現在歐洲中心，長久平衡法國與奧地利的對峙就此終結。第三是法德仇恨與復仇主義：亞爾薩斯與洛林的割讓被法國國民大會以零星票數批准，卻在國內釀成持續數十年的領土要求，帝國議會中阿爾薩斯-洛林代表席位的問題成為每次選舉的爭點，這條線一直延伸到1918年仍未解決。第四是財政與軍制的重整：五十億法郎賠款與佔軍到1873年迫使法國緊縮財政，同時催生1873年的喀琅施塔改組，服役年限延長、徵兵制普及、軍隊規模空前；法國砲兵也在這一時期換裝，七十五毫米野戰砲於1886年定為標準配備，此後三十年裡各國野戰砲口徑幾乎都收攏到七十五毫米這一個數字，德國的八十七毫米則一路沿用到第一次世界大戰。第五是戰爭形態的示範：鐵路動員、電報指揮、針發與沙士孢式後膛步槍、鋼製後膛攻城砲、四個多月的城市圍城與冬季反攻，使普法戰爭成為此後三十年軍事院校與參謀部反覆研究的樣本，同時它也把總體戰的陰影推到桌面，俾斯麥在議會裡承認這場戰爭並非演武，而是以工業動員與鐵路運輸為基礎的國家力量對決。第六是戰後的內政迴響：德國社民黨在1871年拒絕支持和平，把帝國的工資問題推向前台，1878年的反社會主義者法令與1890年代的社會保險制度都由這段經歷催生。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached far beyond the borders of Europe. First came a change of regime: the capture of Napoleon III and the collapse of the Second Empire on 4 September 1870 threw France into the Third Republic, with the Government of National Defence, Trochu's military governorship, the Paris Commune of March 1871 and its suppression, the constitution of 1871 and the presidential election of 1873, and the republican order was thereby fixed. Second, the map of European power was redrawn: on 18 January 1871 the German Empire was proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the Prussian king became German emperor, and a new power built on Rhenish heavy industry, railways and a Prussian-type army appeared at the centre of Europe, ending the long balance between France and Austria. Third came Franco-German bitterness and revanchism: the cession of Alsace and Lorraine was approved by the French National Assembly by a narrow majority, but it bred a territorial claim that ran for decades, and the question of the seats held by the Alsace-Lorraine deputies in the Reichstag became an issue at every election, a thread that was still unresolved in 1918. Fourth, fiscal and military reorganisation: the five billion francs of indemnity and the occupation that lasted until 1873 forced French retrenchment, while at the same time producing the Creuzot reform of 1873, with longer terms of service, universal conscription and an unprecedented size of army; French artillery was rearmed in the same period, and the 75 mm field gun was adopted as standard in 1886, after which for some thirty years the field calibre of almost every army was reduced to that single figure of 75 mm, while Germany kept its 87 mm down to the First World War. Fifth, the war served as a demonstration of the form of warfare itself: mobilisation by rail, command by telegraph, needle guns and Chassepot rifles, steel breech-loading siege guns, four months of siege of a capital and the winter offensive together made the war of 1870 and 1871 a model studied over and over by the staff colleges and war departments of the following thirty years, and at the same time it brought the shadow of total war onto the table, with Bismarck telling the Reichstag that this was no display of arms but a clash of national powers built on industrial mobilisation and rail transport. Sixth came the domestic aftermath: the German Social Democratic party refused to endorse the peace in 1871 and pushed the wage question to the front of imperial politics, and both the Anti-Socialist Law of 1878 and the social insurance system of the 1890s grew out of that experience.
result: 戰局在1871年1月走向終局。1月22日至26日，俾斯麥與法國新政府的代表朱爾·法夫爾在凡爾賽達成停戰協議，1月28日中午生效，法軍放下武器，巴黎與整個法國北部落入德軍佔領；三天之前的1月18日，德意志帝國已在凡爾賽鏡廳宣告成立。5月10日簽訂凡爾賽和約，法國割讓亞爾薩斯與洛林的大部分，賠款五十億法郎，並在賠款付清之前由德軍佔領北部領土。從軍事上看，法軍的有生力量幾乎全滅：拿破崙三世與約十萬人被俘於色當，巴贊內率約十萬人於梅茲投降，布爾巴基的東方軍在貝爾福與埃里庫爾被擊潰或遣散，安貝爾-索恩、羅瓦河與塞納河各軍在冬季戰役中相繼崩潰，巴黎在四個多月的圍城之後於1月28日開城，最後一場大規模會戰是同日的埃里庫爾戰役。戰後的巴黎公社在三月爆發、五月被鎮壓，第三共和國在這一連串打擊下改組國防與軍隊制度，並埋下法德之間綿延半世紀的報復心態。就兵器而言，這場戰爭同時是線膛前膛砲的落幕與新砲兵的開場：卡面這門曾經代表射程優勢的野戰砲，在普法戰役中退居後備與堡壘，會戰的勝負交給克魯伯的鋼製後膛砲與更遠的射距；步兵射速也重寫了會戰節奏，戰後各國爭相仿效沙士孢與針發步槍，砲兵與步兵的射程、射速關係被重新排定，這套秩序一直維持到下一次大規模戰爭。
resultEn: The campaign came to its end in January 1871. Between 22 and 26 January Bismarck and Jules Favre, representing the new French government, reached an armistice at Versailles which took effect at noon on 28 January: the French army laid down its arms, and Paris and the whole north of France passed under German occupation; three days earlier, on 18 January, the German Empire had been proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 10 May: France ceded Alsace and the greater part of Lorraine, agreed an indemnity of five billion francs, and accepted the presence of German troops in the north of the country until the indemnity was paid. Militarily the French army was very nearly annihilated: Napoleon III and about a hundred thousand men were taken at Sedan, Bazaine surrendered some hundred thousand at Metz, the Army of the East under Bourbaki was broken or disbanded around Belfort and Héricourt, the armies of the Vosges, the Loire and the Seine disintegrated in turn during the winter fighting, and Paris opened its gates on 28 January after more than four months of siege, the last large engagement being the battle of Héricourt on the same day. The Paris Commune erupted in March and was crushed in May, and the Third Republic reorganised its national defence and army system under the shock of these successive blows, while a spirit of revenge between France and Germany was sown that would last half a century. As for weapons, the war was at once the funeral of the rifled muzzle-loader and the opening of a new artillery age: the gun on the card face, once the embodiment of superiority in range, was pushed back into reserve batteries and fortresses, and the issue of the battles was decided by Krupp steel breech-loaders firing from greater distances; rates of infantry fire rewrote the rhythm of the engagements, every army afterwards hastened to copy the Chassepot and the needle gun, and the relation of range and rate of fire between artillery and infantry was set in a new order that would hold until the next great war.
